body_text: Hamburg, Germany – Evotec SE (Frankfurt Stock Exchange: EVT, MDAX/TecDAX, Prime Standard, ISIN: DE 000 566480 9, WKN 566480; NASDAQ: EVO) announces that it has updated its revenue guidance for the fiscal year 2025. Guidance on R&D expenses and adjusted EBITDA remains unchanged. For the current fiscal year, the Company expects Group revenues in the range of € 760 – 800 m (previously: € 840 – 880 m; 2024: € 797.0 m); R&D expenditures are expected in a range of € 40 – 50 m (unchanged; 2024: € 50.8 m); Adjusted EBITDA is expected to reach € 30 – 50 m (unchanged; 2024: € 22.6 m). The primary reasons for the refined guidance are a change in the revenue mix and significant cost savings in excess of initial targets set during the Priority Reset. Technology licensing – a key pillar of Evotec’s strategic repositioning – is expected to make a stronger contribution. At the same time, the Shared R&D base business is expected to continue to operate in a challenging market environment in the second half of 2025. Group revenues were below expectations in H1 2025, while adjusted EBITDA was broadly in line with expectations. Actions are underway to transform the business towards sustainable profitable growth. – End of the ad hoc release –

title: Lymph Node Assessment in Veterinary Practice: A Comprehensive Guide to Cytological Evaluation
summary: Lymph node assessment constitutes a fundamental diagnostic modality in veterinary medicine, providing critical pathological data for neoplastic staging, inflammatory disease characterization, and infectious agent identification. Fine-needle aspiration cytology has established itself as a minimally i
body_text: Lymph node assessment constitutes a fundamental diagnostic modality in veterinary medicine, providing critical pathological data for neoplastic staging, inflammatory disease characterization, and infectious agent identification. Fine-needle aspiration cytology has established itself as a minimally invasive, cost-effective diagnostic technique enabling rapid cytomorphological evaluation of lymphadenopathy. This review examines contemporary best practices in lymph node assessment, emphasizing optimal sampling methodologies, systematic cytological interpretation, and integration with advanced diagnostic platforms including digital pathology systems such as Pathview. Recent technological advances in sentinel lymph node mapping and digital cytology have transformed lymph node evaluation protocols, facilitating enhanced precision in staging algorithms and therapeutic decision matrices. Introduction Lymph node cytology represents one of the most frequently utilized diagnostic procedures in veterinary clinical pathology, comprising a substantial proportion of cytological specimens submitted for pathological evaluation (Meichner et al., 2023). This diagnostic modality offers significant advantages over histopathological examination, including rapid turnaround time, minimal invasiveness, and cost-effectiveness, establishing it as an indispensable component of routine diagnostic protocols (Raskin & Meyer, 2010). The clinical significance of precise lymph node assessment has been amplified by developments in precision oncology and targeted immunotherapy. Contemporary therapeutic protocols increasingly require detailed staging data, rendering lymph node evaluation essential for optimal patient management algorithms (Beer et al., 2018). Furthermore, integration of digital pathology platforms has enhanced accessibility and standardization of lymph node cytological interpretation, enabling telepathology consultation and standardized educational resources (Piccione et al., 2025). Anatomy and Physiology of Lymph Nodes Normal Lymph Node Structure Lymph nodes serve as specialized filtration organs within the lymphatic system, designed to trap antigens and facilitate immune responses. Understanding normal lymph node architecture is essential for recognizing pathological changes during cytological evaluation. Normal lymph nodes contain a diverse population of cells, with small lymphocytes comprising 80-90% of the cellular population (Raskin & Meyer, 2010). These cells are characterized by high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, condensed chromatin, and minimal cytoplasm. The remaining cellular population consists of intermediate lymphocytes (10-15%), large lymphocytes or lymphoblasts (2-5%), plasma cells (<5%), and scattered macrophages and dendritic cells. Lymphatic Drainage Patterns Recent advances in sentinel lymph node mapping have highlighted the complexity of lymphatic drainage patterns, demonstrating that regional lymph nodes may not always correspond to the actual draining lymph node (Beer et al., 2018). Computed tomography lymphography has emerged as a valuable alternative to lymphoscintigraphy for sentinel lymph node identification, particularly in cases where radiotracer availability is limited (Ferraris et al., 2023). Indications for Lymph Node Assessment Neoplastic Staging Requirements Lymph node assessment is critical for staging various neoplasms, particularly those demonstrating high metastatic potential. Mast cell tumors, melanomas, histiocytic sarcomas, and most carcinomas require comprehensive lymph node evaluation, even in the absence of palpable lymphadenomegaly (Krick et al., 2009). The sensitivity and specificity of fine-needle aspiration for detecting metastatic disease demonstrate significant variation depending on tumor histotype and sampling methodology. Lymphadenopathy Evaluation Lymphadenopathy may result from reactive hyperplasia, neoplasia (primary or metastatic), inflammatory processes, or infectious etiologies. Systematic cytological evaluation enables differentiation between these pathological entities, directing appropriate therapeutic interventions. Sampling Techniques and Preparation Fine-Needle Aspiration Technique Optimal sampling technique is essential for obtaining diagnostically adequate specimens. The decision between aspiration and non-aspiration techniques depends on the specific characteristics of the target lymph node and the operator's preference. See our article outlining this here . Sample Preparation and Staining Protocols Rapid preparation of high-quality cytological preparations is essential for optimal diagnostic interpretation. The squash preparation technique utilizing two glass slides typically provides optimal cellular morphology and distribution. Romanowsky-type stains (Wright-Giemsa) remain the standard for routine lymph node cytology, providing excellent nuclear chromatin detail and cytoplasmic characteristics. When submitting specimens for external evaluation, inclusion of both stained and unstained slides is essential, as individual pathologists may prefer specific staining protocols for optimal interpretation. Cytological Interpretation Normal Cytological Findings Normal lymph nodes demonstrate a predominance of small lymphocytes with occasional intermediate and large lymphocytes. The presence of tingible body macrophages, which contain phagocytosed nuclear debris, indicates active cellular turnover and is considered a normal finding. Plasma cells may be present in small numbers (<10%) in normal lymph nodes, particularly in nodes draining areas exposed to environmental antigens. The identification of Russell bodies (Mott cells) within plasma cells suggests active antibody production and is not inherently pathological. Reactive Hyperplasia Reactive hyperplasia represents the most common cause of lymphadenopathy in dogs and cats. Cytologically, reactive lymph nodes maintain a mixed population of lymphocytes but show increased numbers of intermediate and large lymphocytes (typically <50% combined). Increased mitotic activity may be observed, but atypical mitotic figures should not be present. The presence of increased plasma cells, particularly those containing Russell bodies, supports a diagnosis of reactive hyperplasia. Tingible body macrophages are often increased in reactive lymph nodes, reflecting enhanced cellular turnover. Inflammatory Patterns Neutrophilic Inflammation When neutrophils comprise >5% of the cellular population, neutrophilic inflammation is present (Baker, 2023; Meichner et al., 2023). This pattern can be associated with bacterial infections, immune-mediated diseases, trauma, or neoplasia. The presence of degenerate neutrophils warrants careful examination for bacterial organisms. Eosinophilic Inflammation Eosinophils comprising >3% of the cellular population indicate eosinophilic inflammation (Baker, 2023; Meichner et al., 2023). This pattern can be associated with hypersensitivity reactions, parasitic infections, or paraneoplastic responses to certain neoplasms, including mast cell tumors and lymphomas. Granulomatous Inflammation The presence of increased macrophages and multinucleated giant cells suggests granulomatous inflammation (Baker, 2023). This pattern often indicates fungal infections, immune-mediated diseases, or foreign body reactions. Careful examination for infectious organisms is essential when this pattern is identified. Neoplastic Changes Primary Lymphoid Neoplasia Lymphoma diagnosis requires identification of a monomorphic population of lymphocytes, typically with increased numbers of large lymphocytes or lymphoblasts. The traditional "rule of 20" suggests that >20% large lymphocytes in a lymph node aspirate supports a diagnosis of lymphoma, though this guideline has limitations. Recent studies have emphasized the importance of phenotyping for accurate lymphoma diagnosis and prognosis. B-cell lymphomas generally have better response rates and longer survival times compared to T-cell lymphomas when treated with conventional chemotherapy protocols. Metastatic Neoplasia The identification of non-lymphoid cells in lymph node aspirates suggests the presence of metastatic disease. Careful attention to cellular morphology, including nuclear characteristics, cytoplasmic features, and cellular arrangements, is essential for identifying metastatic cells. Round cell tumors, including mast cell tumors, plasma cell tumors, and histiocytic neoplasms, can be particularly challenging to differentiate from primary lymphoid neoplasms. The use of cytochemical stains and immunocytochemistry can aid in definitive diagnosis. Advanced Diagnostic Modalities Flow Cytometry Flow cytometry provides valuable information regarding lymphocyte populations and can aid in lymphoma diagnosis and phenotyping. This technique is particularly useful when cytological findings are equivocal or when specific prognostic information is required. Sample preparation for flow cytometry requires special handling, including suspension in appropriate media and rapid processing. Coordination with the testing laboratory is essential to ensure optimal sample quality. Digital Pathology and PathView Integration The integration of digital pathology platforms has revolutionized lymph node cytology education and consultation. PathView and similar platforms enable high-resolution imaging of cytological preparations, facilitating remote consultation and standardized case review. Digital cytology offers several advantages, including improved image quality, enhanced collaboration capabilities, and the ability to create comprehensive case databases for educational purposes. Recent validation studies have demonstrated excellent concordance between digital microscopy and traditional light microscopy for lymph node cytology interpretation (Bonsembiante et al., 2019). Molecular Diagnostics Advanced molecular techniques, including PCR-based assays and next-generation sequencing, are increasingly being applied to lymph node samples. These techniques can provide valuable information regarding clonality, specific genetic mutations, and therapeutic targets. The K9 lymphoma assay represents a significant advancement in canine lymphoma diagnostics, enabling comprehensive genetic profiling of lymphoid neoplasms. This 31-gene panel can identify actionable mutations and provide prognostic information that complements traditional morphological assessment (Marconato et al., 2024). Quality Assurance and Standardization Sample Quality Assessment Adequate sample quality is essential for accurate cytological interpretation. Factors affecting sample quality include proper sampling technique, rapid slide preparation, appropriate staining, and timely evaluation. The development of standardized quality metrics has improved the reliability of lymph node cytology. Inter-observer Variability Studies evaluating inter-observer agreement in lymph node cytology have highlighted the importance of standardized criteria and ongoing education. The use of digital pathology platforms can facilitate standardized training and quality assurance programs. Integration with Clinical Findings Lymph node cytology should always be interpreted in the context of clinical findings, including signalment, history, physical examination, and other diagnostic test results. Close communication between clinicians and pathologists is essential for optimal diagnostic accuracy. Limitations and Pitfalls Sampling Limitations Despite its many advantages, fine-needle aspiration cytology has inherent limitations. The technique samples only a small portion of the lymph node, potentially missing focal lesions or providing unrepresentative samples. In cases where cytological findings are inconsistent with clinical suspicion, histopathological examination should be considered. Interpretation Challenges Certain conditions can be challenging to diagnose cytologically, including indolent lymphomas (marginal zone lymphoma, T-zone lymphoma), early metastatic disease, and specific infectious agents. The development of standardized diagnostic criteria and the integration of ancillary testing can help address these challenges. Species-Specific Considerations Important species differences exist in lymph node cytology interpretation. Feline lymph nodes are more commonly reactive than neoplastic, and in-house diagnosis of feline lymphoma should always be confirmed by a pathologist (Watson et al., 2015). Additionally, breed-specific variations in lymphocyte populations have been reported and should be considered during interpretation (Bexfield et al., 2008). Conclusion Lymph node assessment remains a fundamental component of veterinary diagnostic medicine, providing critical information for disease staging, diagnosis, and treatment planning. The integration of advanced diagnostic modalities, including digital pathology platforms like PathView, has enhanced the accuracy and accessibility of lymph node cytology. Successful lymph node assessment requires a thorough understanding of normal lymph node biology, proper sampling techniques, systematic cytological interpretation, and integration with clinical findings. Ongoing education and quality assurance programs are essential for maintaining diagnostic excellence in this rapidly evolving field. References Baker, K. (2023). title: Inc Magazine: Young Founders Reshaping National Security
summary: Inc Magazine spotlights Usul CEO Jarren Reid as part of a new generation of young founders reshaping national security and the future of defense technology.
body_text: Why Young People Are Building the Future of Defense Inc Magazine just spotlighted Usul CEO Jarren Reid in their feature "Defense Tech's New Guard: They're Young, Patriotic, and Building the Future of Warfare." The piece profiles a new generation of defense founders stepping up as the gap between Silicon Valley's innovation pace and Pentagon procurement cycles creates dangerous capability gaps. At 21, Reid is among the youngest CEOs working with the government today, building infrastructure to close that gap. Connecting DC to Silicon Valley Reid's path to founding Usul is unconventional but intentional. He grew up in Washington D.C. working for defense contractors throughout high school, then dropped out of Stanford to start Usul after seeing firsthand how broken the acquisition process was. "Companies like SpaceX and Palantir set the tone for founders like me to take their chance in the defense industry," Reid told Inc. "They can offer very incentivizing packages to kids, which is a door opener. It brings kids into an industry they might not have considered in the first place." Defense Tech's New Guard This moment matters because it signals a broader shift. Young engineers and builders increasingly see defense as a viable career path where they can make real impact. The article profiles founders like Ethan Thornton (21, Mach Industries) and Andrew Powell (32, Ethos) who are building autonomous weapons systems and pilot training software respectively. What unites this generation isn't just youth. It's the conviction that America's defense technology stack needs to move faster, and that Silicon Valley innovation belongs in national security. As Inc writes: "The future of national defense is intertwined with tech startups and their young founders, who appear poised to remain for the long haul." We're proud to be part of this movement. The defense industrial base needs better infrastructure, and we're building it. Read the full Inc Magazine feature here

title: July Feature Updates: Labeling Agent, Smarter Search, and Editable Rows
summary: This July, we’ve introduced several updates to improve both the speed and precision of your labeling workflow, whether you're reviewing documents, training models, or managing structured data. From sorting lines by metadata to letting AI lend a hand, here’s what’s new.
body_text: Data Studio Labeling Agent: Assigning Models as a Labeler in a Project The new Labeling Agent allows you to assign a model to generate label suggestions automatically, based on the project’s instructions and file content. The agent handles the initial round of labeling, and human reviewers can step in to validate or refine the results, speeding up workflows. Learn more Flexible Edits: Insert Rows in Reviewer Mode In Row Labeling projects, Reviewers can now insert new rows directly into the dataset, making it easier to add missing data or fix alignment issues. Learn more Sort Smarter: Organize Lines by Metadata in Span Labeling You can now sort lines in Span Labeling projects based on metadata attached to each line like timestamps, source IDs, or any custom field. This is especially useful when working with structured documents such as transcripts or logs, helping you stay organized and focus on what matters most. Learn more Targeted Review: Search by Who Labeled or Reviewed in Span Labeling The Search Extension in Span Labeling now enables reviewers to filter labels based on who applied or reviewed them. This makes it easier to focus on results from a specific labeler, double-check another reviewer’s work, or audit model-generated labels, helping ensure higher accuracy and accountability across the projects. Learn more Reusable Search: Save and Reuse Search Queries in Span Labeling The Search Extension now lets you save your search conditions for quick reuse. No need to reconfigure complex conditions each time, simply load your saved search and jump straight to the results. It’s a faster, more efficient way to navigate and manage your data. Learn more These features are now live, try them out and see how they can simplify and speed up your annotation workflows!

title: Product Spotlight: Editable Dashboard Sections
summary: Personalize Your End-User Dashboard Experience
body_text: We’re thrilled to spotlight a highly versatile and user-friendly feature: Editable Dashboard Sections . This feature allows your users to create their own dashboard with a library of charts that you’ve defined. Create a standard template to start, and your users can add/remove charts and reformat the dashboard to show the most relevant metrics for their own organization. With Editable Dashboards, we’ve bridged the gap between our standard Dashboards and Report Builder , providing your users with the ability to create their own dashboard without needing to create their own charts from scratch. Editable Dashboard Sections 101 Here are the key features and functionality you need to know about: Versatile Placement Editable Sections can be seamlessly integrated into an existing dashboard or used as a standalone dashboard. This versatility ensures that you can adapt it to fit perfectly within your current workflow or create a new, dedicated space for your custom data views. Flexible Functionality Enjoy the freedom to edit details and layouts according to your needs. Whether you’re fine-tuning specific elements or reimagining the entire layout, Editable Sections offer the flexibility to make it happen. Customizable Charts Choose from a variety of charts and visualizations to best represent your data. This feature allows you to tailor the presentation to suit different audiences and purposes, ensuring that your data is always communicated effectively. User-Level Customization Editable Sections support customization at both the end-user level and the tenant level. This means you can provide a personalized experience for individual users or implement consistent customization across your entire application. Create Unique Experiences The highly flexible nature of Editable Sections allows you to create a variety of unique experiences. Whether you need a detailed analytical dashboard or a simple overview, this feature can accommodate your requirements. User-Friendly Design Designed with non-technical users in mind, Editable Sections make it easy for everyone to create and customize dashboards. No specialized skills are required, empowering all users to take full advantage of this powerful feature. Export data Share data on the custom dashboard or export the entire dashboard. Explo support CSV, Excel, PDF, and image exports. Why We Recommend Using Editable Sections With Editable Sections, you have the power to offer a personalized end-user experience without overwhelming users with raw data. Seamless Integration : Editable Sections fit effortlessly into your existing workflow, providing a streamlined experience without disruptions. Personalized Experiences : Offer tailored experiences for individual users or consistent customization across your application, enhancing user satisfaction and engagement. Versatility and Engagement : Adapt your dashboards to various use cases, making them more engaging and effective for your specific needs. Empowerment for All Users : Enable all end-users to create and customize dashboards, regardless of their technical expertise, fostering a more inclusive and productive environment. How to Use Editable Sections Using Editable Sections is straightforward and designed to be user-friendly, even for non-technical users. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you get started: Step 1: Access the Feature Navigate to the page or dashboard where you want to add an Editable Section. Look for the option to add or edit sections in your dashboard settings. Step 2: Choose Placement Decide whether you want to integrate the Editable Section into an existing page or create a new standalone dashboard. Select the appropriate option based on your needs. Step 3: Customize Layout and Details Use the intuitive drag-and-drop interface to arrange the layout of your section. You can add, remove, and resize various elements to fit your desired structure. Edit the details of each component, such as text, images, and data inputs, to ensure everything aligns with your requirements. Step 4: Select Visualizations Choose from a range of charts and visualizations to represent your data. Simply drag the desired chart type into your section and configure the data sources and display settings. Step 5: User-Level Customization Decide if you want the section to be customizable at the end-user level or the tenant level. Enable user-level customization to allow individual users to personalize their own dashboards, or apply settings universally for consistent branding and layout. Step 6: Save and Share Once you’re satisfied with your Editable Section, save your changes. You can then share the section as an image file or CSV, making it easy to distribute and collaborate with others. Step 7: Continuous Improvement Editable Sections are designed to be flexible, so you can continuously improve and update them as needed. Regularly review and refine your sections to keep them relevant and effective. Tips for Maximizing the Use of Editable Sections Experiment with Layouts : Try different layouts to find the most effective way to present your data. Engage Users : Encourage users to personalize their sections to enhance engagement and satisfaction. Stay Consistent : Maintain consistent branding across all sections to reinforce your brand identity. Utilize Custom Visuals : Leverage the variety of available charts and visualizations to keep your data presentations dynamic and informative. By following these steps, you can make the most of Editable Sections, creating powerful, customized dashboards that enhance your data presentation and user experience. If your users are looking for a full self-service experience where they can dive into the data and create their own visualizations from scratch, check out our Report Builder Product . Start exploring this feature today and unlock the full potential of your dashboards! ‍

body_text: View All News Hawthorn Bancshares Reports Second Quarter 2025 Results July 30, 2025 Download (opens in new window) JEFFERSON CITY, Mo., July 30, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hawthorn Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: HWBK) , (the “Company”), the bank holding company for Hawthorn Bank, reported second quarter 2025 net income of $6.1 million, or earnings per diluted share (“EPS”) of $0.88. Second Quarter 2025 Results Net income improved $1.5 million, or 31.8% , to $6.1 million from the second quarter 2024 (the "prior year quarter") and the efficiency ratio improved to 62.32% compared to 66.24% for the prior year quarter EPS of $0.88 , an improvement of $0.22 per share, or 33% , from the prior year quarter Net interest margin, fully taxable equivalent ("FTE") improved in the second quarter 2025 to 3.89% compared to 3.67% for first quarter 2025 (the "prior quarter”) Provision for credit losses were $0.3 million higher than the prior quarter and $0.5 million lower than the prior year quarter Return on average assets and equity of 1.36% and 15.85%, respectively Loans decreased $7.4 million, or 0.5%, and deposits decreased $25.9 million , or 1.7% , compared to the prior quarter Investments increased $2.8 million, or 1.2%, compared to the prior quarter Credit quality remained strong with non-performing assets to total loans of 0.35% improving from 0.54% in the prior year quarter Remained well capitalized with total risk-based capital of 15.12% Book Value per share increased $2.83 to $22.53 , or 14.3% , compared to the prior year quarter Brent Giles, Chief Executive Officer of Hawthorn Bancshares, Inc. commented, “As a team, during the second quarter, I am proud of what we accomplished towards our strategic goals. The contributions across the Bank truly embodied our "One Hawthorn" spirit. I am also pleased with our financial results for the second quarter. Managing our net interest margin in highly competitive markets and controlling expenses were top initiatives during the quarter. Our strong results reflect the focus on these areas." EPS improved to $0.88 for the second quarter 2025 compared to $0.77 for the prior quarter and $0.66 for the prior year quarter. Net income for the six months ended June 30, 2025 was $11.5 million, or $1.65 per diluted share, an increase of $2.4 million compared to $9.1 million, or $1.29 per diluted share, for the six months ended June 30, 2024. Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin Net interest income for the second quarter 2025 was $16.1 million, an increase of $0.8 million from the prior quarter, and an increase of $2.0 million from the prior year quarter. Non-interest Income Total non-interest income for the second quarter 2025 was $3.5 million, an increase of $0.1 million, or 2.4%, from the prior quarter, and a decrease of $0.5 million, or 11.3%, from the prior year quarter. Non-interest income was consistent at $7.0 million for both the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Non-interest Expense Total non-interest expense for the second quarter 2025 was $12.3 million, a decrease of $0.2 million, or 1.8%, from the prior quarter, and an increase of $0.2 million, or 2.0%, from the prior year quarter. For the six months ended June 30, 2025, non-interest expense was $24.8 million, an increase of $0.2 million as compared to $24.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2024. The improvement in the current quarter compared to the prior quarter was primarily due to higher net interest margin and lower non-interest expenses in the current quarter. Investments Investments increased $2.8 million, or 1.2%, to $229.4 million as of June 30, 2025 compared to March 31, 2025, and increased $38.2 million, or 20.0%, from June 30, 2024. Non-performing assets totaled $5.2 million at June 30, 2025, compared to $3.1 million and $8.1 million at March 31, 2025 and June 30, 2024, respectively. The increase in non-performing assets in the current quarter compared to the prior quarter was the result of the Company closing an operational center and moving the property to other real estate owned. In the second quarter 2025, the Company had net loan charge-offs of $0.05 million, or 0.01% annualized, of average loans, compared to net loan charge-offs of $0.02 million, or 0.00% of average loans, and $1.98 million, or 0.53% annualized, of average loans, in the prior quarter and prior year quarter, respectively. The allowance for credit losses at June 30, 2025 was $21.6 million, or 1.47% of outstanding loans, and 781.24% of non-performing loans. At March 31, 2025, the allowance for credit losses was $21.8 million, or 1.48% of outstanding loans, and 885.01% of non-performing loans. At June 30, 2024, the allowance for credit losses was $22.0 million, or 1.47% of outstanding loans, and 495.38% of non-performing loans. The allowance for credit losses represents management’s best estimate of expected losses inherent in the loan portfolio and is commensurate with risks in the loan portfolio as of June 30, 2025 as determined by management. Deposits Total deposits at June 30, 2025 were $1.5 billion, a decrease of $25.9 million, or 1.7%, from March 31, 2025, and a decrease of $32.3 million, or 2.1% annualized, from June 30, 2024. The decrease in deposits at June 30, 2025 as compared to June 30, 2024 was primarily a result of an decrease in savings, interest checking and money market accounts. Capital The Company maintains its “well capitalized” regulatory capital position. At June 30, 2025, capital ratios were as follows: total risk-based capital to risk-weighted assets 15.12%; tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets 13.87%; tier 1 leverage 11.87%; and common equity to assets 8.35%. Pursuant to the Company's Repurchase Plan, management is given discretion to determine the number and pricing of the shares to be purchased under the plan, as well as the timing of any such purchases. The Board Directors amended the plan on June 3, 2025 and approved increasing the authorized repurchase limit to $10 million. title: Introducing the Hubble Bluetooth® Finding Network
summary: Connect a Bluetooth device to a global satellite network, delivering affordable, low-power tracking and monitoring for diverse industrial and commercial ...
body_text: We just launched something I've wanted to build for a long time: A global Bluetooth® Low Energy (LE) finding network that gives enterprises the same power that Apple’s Find My, Google’s Find My Device, and Samsung’s SmartThings Find gave to consumers. But unlike those networks, Hubble’s Bluetooth Terrestrial Network is built specifically for businesses with full control, zero infrastructure, and global scale baked in from the start. Today we’re also launching hubble.com . If you’re a developer or enterprise looking to integrate Bluetooth into your products or operations, you can join our waitlist and get access to the network right away. What We Built Consumer networks proved how powerful Bluetooth can be for tracking and discovery. But they were never built for enterprise. They’re closed ecosystems. They don’t give you your data. And you’re subject to their rules. We’ve flipped the model. The Hubble Terrestrial Network gives you: Global Coverage : We’re live today across 88 million+ passive scanners , phones, gateways, and infrastructure already deployed in homes, cities, highways, warehouses, and more. Zero Infrastructure : No hardware. No installers. Just update your Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) advertisement format. You’re live in minutes. Full Ownership : You own the devices, the data, the APIs, the analytics. Secure by Design : Rotating IDs, encrypted payloads, verified endpoints, we built this for enterprise use from day one. Open SDKs & APIs : Developer-first integration, no proprietary lock-in. What You Can Do With It This is a finding network that actually works for the real world: Asset Tracking – Pallets, tools, containers, equipment. Fleet Management – Know what’s in each vehicle or trailer, in real time. Cold Chain Monitoring – Combine Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) sensors with location telemetry. Workplace Safety – Track badges or wearables in hazardous areas. Equipment Sharing – Enable shared access, usage data, and location history across sites. And we’re just scratching the surface. It’s Live And You Can Build on It Now If you want to start building with the network, we’re now onboarding early developers and customers. Visit docs.hubble.com There, you’ll find technical details, architecture, and access to our waitlist. If you’re ready to build, we’ll get you in fast. We’ve already seen Fortune 500s use this platform to track assets at scale with no added infrastructure. We’re opening up that same power to the rest of the world. What’s Next In March 2024, Hubble became the first to connect a Bluetooth device directly to a satellite. That breakthrough changed the game. Our vision is simple: Connect billions of Bluetooth devices everywhere on Earth, even off the grid. Today’s launch is a huge step toward that. If you want to be part of it as a developer, a partner, or just someone curious, check out hubble.com and join the network. Let’s build something big.

title: The Game Theory of Recruiting
summary: Dover transforms recruiting from a high-cost, low-trust game into an efficient marketplace where startups pay $2k-$8k per hire instead of 20-30% agency fees through aligned incentives and transparency.
body_text: Dover re‑engineers the game’s payoff structure so that even a small startup can reach the high‑reward equilibrium without committing to a full‑time recruiter. Public cost‑per‑hire data. Dover logs every hire publicly. Recruiters’ average cost per hire becomes common knowledge. Because their future business depends on these numbers, recruiters choose strategies that minimize cost: sharing candid feedback, refining specs early, and pivoting when a search stalls. Minute‑by‑minute billing. In Dover’s marketplace, employers pay recruiters based on an agreed hourly rate. This forces companies to reveal their intent: serious founders are happy to pay people to work for them while tire‑kickers self‑select out. Because recruiters on Dover’s marketplace bill hourly and there aren’t any long‑term contracts, startups retain full flexibility. Cross‑account penalties. If a company is dissatisfied and “fires” a recruiter on Dover’s marketplace, that recruiter’s revenue shrinks across all their other Dover engagements. The threat of lost future earnings keeps recruiters honest and discourages them from taking on searches they can’t fill. These mechanisms replicate the benefits of a repeated game, like trust, transparency and optimizing for the future, without requiring a full‑time hire. In equilibrium, both founders and recruiters have incentives to cooperate: founders provide clear specs and quick feedback; recruiters work efficiently and truthfully. Dover’s marketplace data shows that most hires close between $2k and $8k, an order of magnitude cheaper than traditional agencies, while still preserving the flexibility of contingency recruiting.

title: Oracle and Bloom Energy Collaborate to Deliver Power to Data Centers at the Speed of AI
summary: Bloom and Oracle collaborate to deliver onsite power to Oracle AI data centers within 90 days Fuel cells will support Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s growth strategy with clean, reliable, and cost-efficient power for large-scale AI workloads SAN JOSE, Calif. – July 24, 2025 –Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), a global leader in power solutions, today announced that […]
body_text: Bloom and Oracle collaborate to deliver onsite power to Oracle AI data centers within 90 days Fuel cells will support Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s growth strategy with clean, reliable, and cost-efficient power for large-scale AI workloads SAN JOSE, Calif. – July 24, 2025 –Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), a global leader in power solutions, today announced that it will deploy its fuel cell technology at select Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) data centers in the U.S. To support the growing demand for OCI’s AI and cloud computing services, Bloom Energy will deliver highly reliable and cost-efficient onsite power for an entire data center within 90 days. “We continue to see strong global demand for OCI services across our entire data center portfolio including our large gigawatt AI data centers,” said Mahesh Thiagarajan, Executive Vice President, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure . “Customers expect to run their AI workloads and new AI applications at peak performance. Bloom’s fuel cell technology will join OCI’s extensive energy portfolio, further supporting our cutting-edge AI infrastructure with reliable, clean power that can be quickly deployed and easily scaled.” “Oracle Cloud Infrastructure requires power solutions engineered to meet the performance and reliability demands of today’s most advanced AI and compute workloads,” said Aman Joshi, Chief Commercial Officer of Bloom Energy . “This significant collaboration provides Oracle with ultra-reliable, clean, and cost-efficient power that supports its growth strategy with the speed and certainty it needs.” Bloom’s systems also deliver clean power with virtually no air pollution and no water use, contributing to Oracle’s use of sustainable energy sources to power Oracle Cloud. Bloom Energy’s energy solutions power the world’s most critical digital infrastructure, following agreements with Equinix , American Electric Power (AEP) , and Quanta Computing . To date, Bloom Energy has deployed over 400 MW to power data centers worldwide. About Bloom Energy Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell system provides ultra-resilient, highly scalable onsite electricity generation for Fortune 500 companies around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities, and other commercial and industrial sectors. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Bloom Energy has deployed 1.5 GW of low-carbon power across more than 1,200 installations globally. For more information, visit www.BloomEnergy.com . title: Humans of Prodigal - Suryansh Singh -
summary: Suryansh Singh joined Prodigal in 2024 and is a Strategy and Ops Lead, heading the Digital Execution vertical. He brings a problem-solving mindset and analytical rigour from his previous consulting experience.
body_text: Suryansh Singh joined Prodigal in 2024 and is a Strategy and Ops Lead, heading the Digital Execution vertical. He brings a problem-solving mindset and analytical rigour from his previous consulting experience. Where did you grow up, and where are you based now? I’ve spent my entire life in Mumbai, right from school to college. My job at Prodigal, brought me to Bangalore, where the Digital Execution (DEE) team and I are currently based. What’s your educational background, and what were your previous work experiences before joining Prodigal? I studied Mechanical Engineering at IIT Bombay, but my time there was less about engineering and more about exploring different interests. I was part of the racing team, dabbled in machine learning projects, participated in the Literary Arts Club focusing on quizzing and board games, and was involved in the student mentorship program. I’ve always had the urge to explore new things, and that’s what led me to my first job in consulting. I joined YCP Auctus immediately after college and spent 1 year and 5 months there. I worked on projects in both Mumbai and Gurgaon, primarily in the airport sector. It was an exciting experience, but over time, I realized that my idea of consulting and the reality of it started to diverge. While I initially enjoyed learning new things, I didn’t like the multiple layers of corporate decision-making. The impact of my work would take a long time to materialize, and I wanted something more direct, hands-on, and impactful. What attracted you to join Prodigal, and how has your role evolved since you started? I had a couple of close friends who had been raving about Prodigal throughout my final year, so I already knew about the company. The first thing that attracted me was the people. I saw that the team here was incredibly strong, and I’d heard great things about the culture. But what truly convinced me was my initial conversation with Raag, who I now work with. He described a role where my work would directly impact the business, and I’d have full ownership and responsibility for my projects. That level of responsibility excited me. Prodigal was at the perfect maturity level for me. It wasn’t too early-stage where the job would be vague and chaotic, but it also wasn’t a large, bureaucratic company where corporate culture would start creeping in. The DEE team was still relatively new, and I saw a lot of scope to build and innovate. That was exactly what I was looking for. Can you share a significant project or achievement you’re proud of during your time here? One of the most exciting projects I worked on was optimizing a client’s dialer strategy as part of our omnichannel outreach efforts. Instead of spamming everyone with calls, we focused on identifying the right people to call and the best time to reach them. This ensured that we weren’t harassing customers who didn’t want to be called but instead were targeting those who were likely to respond. The impact was massive, we saw a 30-40% increase in payments collected. It was particularly satisfying because the results were a direct outcome of my work, not just one factor among many. We started with an A/B test, comparing our strategy against the client’s existing approach, and the difference was clear. The client was so happy with the results that they decided to end the test early and fully adopt our approach. That kind of validation is incredibly rewarding. What are your favorite hobbies or activities outside of work? I’m a huge football enthusiast. I love playing, watching, and even playing FIFA. Football is a big part of my life. I’m also deeply into quizzing. I was very active in college and continued when I moved to Gurgaon, where I was one of the founding members of a quiz club. I love the mix of problem-solving and random trivia, as it keeps my curiosity alive. Do you have any personal projects or passions you’re currently pursuing? I’ve been looking for a good quiz club in Bangalore to join so I can stay involved in the community and meet like-minded people. More recently, I also picked up pickleball. Once I’m back in Bangalore, I want to play more regularly. Which of Prodigal’s values resonates with you the most, and why? I’d say Bias for Action. One thing Shantanu once told me really stuck: we often assume that every suggestion is a strict rule, but in reality, some things are just guidelines. Understanding that distinction allows us to move faster. Also, when I'm able to pull things off in this manner, I get a distinct rush that is incredibly rewarding. That mindset doesn’t always come naturally to me, but I’m working on applying it more often. Is there an interesting fact about yourself that your colleagues might not know? During my final semester of college, I checked off a bucket-list goal by going blonde. I haven't experimented since then, but blue seems like an exciting next step - maybe I'll give it a shot someday!

title: Postbiotics: The Next Frontier in Microbiome Health
summary: Discover how postbiotics support your microbiome and your health.
body_text: Postbiotics: The Next Frontier in Microbiome Health The human body is full of bacteria. Believe it or not—this is a good thing. Living microbial communities play a vital role in human health. These “microbiomes” can be found in the gut, the skin, the mouth, the respiratory tract, and more. Over the past couple decades, scientists have made numerous discoveries about how the microbiome works and the many ways it benefits health. Most of this work focused on the intestine, but research suggests that some of the knowledge we’ve gained could benefit other microbiomes in the body. Probiotics, living microorganisms that benefit gut health, emerged from the initial scientific discoveries about the microbiome and quickly became one of the most popular supplements consumed in the world. As the science developed, the focus broadened to include prebiotics , the variety of fibers that act as gut microbiome fertilizer. Recently, a new biotechnology has started to hit the shelves: post biotics. In this article, we’ll discuss everything you need to know about these beneficial byproducts. What are Postbiotics? Postbiotics are the byproducts of the natural metabolic process (fermentation) of probiotic bacteria. They include various types of molecules such as short-chain fatty acids, peptides, organic acids, enzymes, and more. They offer many of the same benefits that probiotics do. But there’s one key difference. Postbiotics are non-living bioactive metabolites. While probiotics are live strains of bacteria. There are three similar words that frequently come up when discussing the microbiome, each with its own unique definition: probiotics, prebiotics, and postbiotics. Let’s clarify the difference between each term: Probiotics: Unlike the following two terms, probiotics are living microorganisms. Basically, they’re the “good” microbes living in your gut. You can bring more probiotics into your body by eating probiotic foods such as yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut, and kimchi—or quality probiotic supplements. Prebiotics: Like all living things, your microbes need to eat. Prebiotics are the substances that the microbes in your body consume for sustenance . These include starches, inulin, and pectin—all forms of complex carbohydrates. Postbiotics: When probiotic bacteria metabolize their food, they create various byproducts. These byproducts can offer you some of the same benefits as the microbes themselves and are called postbiotics. Postbiotics don’t require the use of live bacteria. They’re stable, safe, and have a broad range of application in health products. You might start to notice them in nutraceuticals, foods, supplements, and even high-end skincare products. Let’s dive a little deeper into some of the practical applications of postbiotics. The Gut Biome: A Vital Microbial Ecosystem One of the most well-researched healthy bacterial communities is the gut biome. When your gut microbiome is healthy, it helps your body digest food, regulate immune function, guard against harmful pathogens, and support cognitive functions through the gut-brain axis . Although the exact composition of each person’s gut biome is different, they are all composed of the same types of microorganisms: bacteria, viruses, and fungi. When people talk about a functioning microbiome, they often use descriptors like “healthy” and “balanced.” So, what does it actually mean for your microbiome to be healthy? A healthy gut biome is one in which there are plenty of the good microorganisms and inconsequential amounts of the bad. This is exactly how probiotics work. They improve gut health by increasing the number of beneficial bacteria and reducing the number of harmful bacteria to make your microbiome healthier. Basically, a healthy or balanced microbiome is able to do its job—and if it’s not, you’ll probably notice. An unbalanced gut biome is called dysbiosis and can have a number of adverse health effects. These include irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), autoimmune disorders, and even new allergies. Needless to say, it’s important to care for your gut biome. Postbiotics do many of the same things as probiotics—without live strains of bacteria. They support the growth and the function of healthy bacteria in your gut microbiome, which supports your health. This means that postbiotics shift the composition of the microbiome towards a healthier, more balanced ecosystem. Postbiotic metabolites also have direct benefits for the gut. They’ve been shown to: Regulate digestion and absorption of nutrients Support the intestinal barrier Suppress bad bacteria Fight pathogens Play a role in the gut-brain axis Reduce irritation in the gut So how do you increase the amount of postbiotics in your gut? Like with all things health-related—it starts with your diet. Dietary Sources of Prebiotics, Probiotics, and Postbiotics Your body naturally produces postbiotics as the bacteria in your gut metabolize their food and create waste. You can increase the amount of postbiotics in your system by increasing the amount of probiotics and prebiotics that you consume. The formula is pretty simple: the more food (prebiotics) you supply to the microorganisms (probiotics) in your gut biome, the more byproducts (postbiotics) they will create. Foods that are rich in probiotics are typically fermented foods, which include: Kefir Cottage cheese Kimchi Kombucha Buttermilk Sauerkraut High fiber foods tend to be the best source of prebiotics. Some examples of prebiotic-rich foods include: Barley Garlic Oats Seaweed Flax seed Onions If you are looking to directly supply your body with more postbiotics, those supplements exist as well. But some of the most interesting applications for postbiotics are those that wouldn’t be practical for probiotic bacteria. Let’s discuss how the benefits of postbiotics translate to another important microbiome: your skin flora. Skin Microbiome: Your Body’s Natural Barrier The skin microbiome is the community of microorganisms; bacteria, fungi, and viruses, that live on the skin. Just like the gut microbiome, this microbial community is much more than a passive, fellow traveler. The skin flora plays a vital role in maintaining skin health and even other aspects of health. Here are some of the roles your skin microbiome is involved in: Protection of the Skin: A healthy skin flora inhibits the growth of potential invaders and pathogens on the skin. Skin Barrier Function: Your skin microbiome acts as a functional barrier, helping the skin retain moisture, improve hydration, and reduce skin sensitivity. Immune Support: The skin flora interacts with the immune system to support balanced inflammatory responses. Tissue Healing: A balanced skin microbiome promotes tissue repair and cell turnover on the skin while preventing infection in vulnerable areas. Skin Health and Beauty: A strong and healthy skin flora is associated with a balanced complexion and clear, moisturized skin. Dysbiosis occurs when the skin microbiome is out of balance or disrupted. This can lead to a variety of skin issues like acne, redness, dermatitis, and infections. In fact, skin sensitivity and problematic skin are related to a damaged skin microbiome. Maintaining a healthy skin flora involves taking care of your skin, avoiding harsh chemicals in skincare products, and choosing products that support a healthy microbial balance on the skin. That’s where postbiotics come in. Postbiotics can support the good bacteria on the skin by feeding it with beneficial metabolites. That’s why many skincare products now include postbiotics. Using postbiotics on the skin will support all the benefits we mentioned above. They can improve the skin’s barrier function, reduce acne and skin sensitivity, improve hydration, balance the pH of the skin, and even reduce signs of aging like visible fine lines and discoloration. In Summary Science has discovered so much in recent years about the symbiotic microbial communities in the human body. But we are still barely scratching the surface. Although much of the research has been focused on the gut microbiome, the biotechnology of postbiotics represents a new frontier. Where the discoveries made about the gut microbiome can be applied in completely new contexts. The years to come will undoubtedly lead to more discoveries and a better understanding of the body’s less-explored microbiomes in overall health. References https://www.webmd.com/digestive-disorders/features/what-are-postbiotics https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/what-are-postbiotics https://health.clevelandclinic.org/postbiotics https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/postbiotics Submit a Question https://askthescientists.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/AdobeStock_578273463.jpeg 567 850 staff staff 2025-07-30 20:20:30 2025-08-01 08:41:53 Postbiotics: The Next Frontier in Microbiome Health

title: Interoperability in home climate control
summary: At UEI, interoperability is our foundation, we’ve built an extensive knowledge base of device control protocols, ensuring connectivity across devices.
body_text: For a thermostat to be truly smart, it takes more than an app and connection to the cloud — it must communicate with a wide variety of devices. While heating systems are the primary focus, including gas heaters, heat pumps, mini-split air conditioning units and electric heaters, but also district heating or block heating; smart thermostats often control cooling and ventilation systems as well. Compatibility with multiple fuel sources such as electricity, natural gas, oil, or propane is also essential, especially in diverse markets where flexibility matters most At UEI, interoperability is our foundation. It’s why we’re called Universal Electronics . For nearly 40 years, we’ve built an extensive knowledge base of device control protocols, starting with remotes for TVs and home-entertainment systems. In the last two decades, we have expanded to HVAC, smart home electronics and IoT ensuring seamless connectivity across an ever-growing ecosystem of devices. Our TIDE Dial and TIDE Touch smart thermostats are engineered for seamless interoperability. At UEI, we are dedicated to ensuring our products integrate effortlessly with any HVAC system, no matter the brand, protocol, power source, or heat exchange system. The TIDE Family is also designed for Demand Response systems, helping utilities balance peak loads on an increasingly strained grid. Powered by QuickSet , our thermostats seamlessly integrate with a wide range of Zigbee devices – including sensors and thermostatic radiator valves, to enhance both sustainability and comfort. By adapting to users’ daily routines, our intelligent energy management tools simplify efficiency without sacrificing convenience. With our Interoperability as a Service offering, TIDE products effortlessly connect the existing smart home ecosystems, including hubs, smart speakers, and automation systems. Stay tuned for an upcoming blog post that will dive deeper into these capabilities. Even major tech companies have tried — and failed — to serve the European smart thermostat market due to its overwhelming complexity. The challenge lies in supporting a fragmented ecosystem, each country has its own mix of HVAC brands, protocols shaped by local regulations and diverse heating sources. With millions of smart thermostats deployed globally for HVAC market leaders, we have mastered the art of seamless climate control. Our portfolio spans handheld to wall-mounted controllers, from Infrared to advanced wireless RF, and from tactile keys to intuitive touchscreens. But what really sets us apart is our expertise in interoperability standards like Zigbee and Matter, bridging the gap between HVAC systems and the smart home. We are redefining energy management by integrating devices into a cohesive, intelligent ecosystem that optimizes comfort, efficiency, and sustainability. Ready to explore how our interoperability expertise can transform your approach to HVAC control and smart energy? Contact us.

title: High-Trend International Group Held Extraordinary General Meeting for Share Capital Restructure

body_text: SINGAPORE , July 17, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- High-Trend International Group (the "Registrant" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: HTCO ), a global ocean technology company, held its Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (the "Meeting") on July 16, 2025 . At the Meeting, the shareholders voted to approve (1) the proposal that effective immediately following the close of the Meeting, every 25 issued and unissued class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0001 each and every 25 issued and unissued class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0001 each in the Company's existing share capital be consolidated into 1 class A ordinary share of a par value of US$0.0025 and 1 class B ordinary share of a par value of US$0.0025 , respectively (each a "Consolidated Share") and such Consolidated Shares shall rank pari passu in all respects with each other and have the rights and privileges and be subject to the restrictions as contained in the third amended and restated memorandum and articles of association of the Company (the "Share Consolidation"), so that immediately following the Share Consolidation, the authorized share capital of the Company shall be changed from US$50,000 divided into 497,500,000 class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0001 each and 2,500,000 class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0001 each, to US$50,000 divided into 19,900,000 class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each and 100,000 class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each; (2) the proposal that effective immediately following the close of the Meeting, the authorized share capital of the Company be increased by the creation of an additional 470,000,000 class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each and 10,000,000 class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each to rank pari passu in all respects with the existing class A ordinary shares and class B ordinary shares, respectively (the "Increase of Authorized Share Capital") so that immediately following the Increase of Authorized Share Capital, the authorized share capital of the Company shall be changed from US$50,000 divided into 19,900,000 class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each and 100,000 class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each, to US$1,250,000 divided into 489,900,000 class A ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each and 10,100,000 class B ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0025 each; and (3) the proposal that effective immediately following the close of the Meeting, the second amended and restated memorandum and articles of association of the Company currently in effect be amended and restated by the deletion in their entirety and the substitution in their place of the third amended and restated memorandum and articles of association annexed to the notice of the Meeting. About High-Trend International Group High-Trend International Group ("High-Trend" or the "Company") is a global ocean technology company with businesses in international shipping and marine carbon neutrality. The Company connects the decarbonization needs of the maritime industry with the supply of the carbon finance market through technology ecosystem, creating a new paradigm for maritime sustainability. title: 🚀 Product Update: Document Relationships and Entities
summary: Docsum’s July 2025 product update introduces Document Relationships and Entity Management, transforming contract lifecycle management for legal, finance, and operations teams in the United States and worldwide. With Document Relationships, users can explicitly link related contracts—including Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Order Forms, Amendments, Renewals, and Terminations—creating a connected contract repository that makes it easy to answer questions like “Is this agreement still active?” or “Which documents are tied to this MSA?” The new Entity Management feature organizes all counterparty data, such as legal names, signers, addresses, and entity types (Vendor, Customer, Internal), allowing businesses to search, filter, and report on every agreement tied to a specific partner. By centralizing contract and counterparty tracking, Docsum reduces risk, streamlines compliance, and gives companies a single source of truth for audit-ready, modern contract management.
body_text: Not all contracts stand alone. A Master Service Agreement spawns a dozen Order Forms. A Renewal quietly extends a deal. A Termination redefines what was once active. Until now, these connections were invisible unless you remembered them or kept your own spreadsheet. That changes today. 🔗 Document Relationships: View Contracts in Context Know how your contracts connect. With this release, Docsum introduces two powerful features: Document Relationships and Entities. See how agreements relate, track which ones are still in force, and understand who you are doing business with, all in one place. Need to know if an Order Form is still active? Want to see if there is a Termination for a specific agreement? Instead of relying on naming conventions or tribal knowledge, you can now create explicit, bidirectional links between contracts in Docsum. Use the “Relate” action in the toolbar to link any documents—MSAs, Order Forms, Amendments, Renewals, and more. Then, navigate to the “Related Documents” tab on a contract sheet to view connected documents at a glance. Whether you are tracking a long negotiation thread or surfacing the latest version of an agreement, you can now see the full picture in one place. No more asking “Is this the latest version?” or “Did we ever terminate this agreement?” The relationships are right there in Docsum. Directional relationship types and automatic linking are coming soon. 🏢 Entities: Structure Your Contract Counterparties Understand your counterparties, clearly. Docsum has always extracted counterparty details from contracts based on your internal entities but we didn't have a dedicated place for all entity information. With the new Entities feature, we now offer a full system of record for entities across all your contracts both internal and external. Search, filter, and report based on structured data like: Legal name Signer(s) Addresses Entity type (Vendor, Customer, Partner, Internal, etc.) One of the most powerful views? The “Contracts” tab on an entity profile, where you can see all agreements tied to that party, perfect for answering questions like: “What contracts have we signed with Acme Inc.?” Now, you can simply search for “Acme Inc.” and see the full list. This view will be automatically populated for accounts created during onboarding and through contract data extraction. Our mission to be the best contract repository on the market Most CLM is riddled with complex workflow management and pre-signature configurations that are relatively similar. What they have all truly lacked is the ability to improve and respond to precedent that are changing in real-time. As we re-think contract lifecycle management, we believe that it needs to be informed and molded by historical context. The only way to do this is starting with a deep index of all your agreements and next by a clear representation of how they are related and how these commercial and legal obligations are solidified between you and your counterparties. We are doubling down on correlating this by specific Entities so you'll be able to ask more nuanced questions like: "What are all the amendments we've historically signed with this customer? Provide a summary of key changes." "What discounts and sales concessions have we previously received from this vendor so we can improve our negotiation." "Can we sync all related documents with related Opportunity records in Salesforce from Docsum?" We are excited by our upcoming releases and invite you to share your feedback on how this can better fit your unique legal, revops, or finance reporting needs.

Improving Accessory Recommendations with LLMs at Target
summary: An article by David Relyea, Rankyung Park, Alina Nesen, Longjiang Yang, AJ Dabruzzi, and Amit Pande : This GenAI-based algorithm makes it easier than ever to pair the right accessory with the right product.
body_text: Accessories! Whether it’s batteries for a toy, a case for a phone, or the perfect end table to complement a living room set, guests want to know which items go well together. However, providing high-quality accessory recommendations is a complex challenge, especially because of the sheer volume of our catalog and the many item attributes that might matter. Depending on the product, guests might prioritize color, kid-friendliness, flavor, material, brand—or any of a hundred other features. To address this challenge, the Product Recommendations Team was recently asked to create a “related accessory” algorithm for both our Electronics and Home categories. Thanks to the power of Large Language Models (LLMs), we developed GRAM, a GenAI-based Related Accessory Model, for Home. It’s a scalable and performant algorithm that makes it easier than ever to pair the right accessory with the right product. Technical Challenges We faced three key technical challenges that significantly impacted the effectiveness of our system as we set out to design it. 1. Determining Attribute Importance: Our first challenge was identifying the importance of all attributes across each category. Given our vast catalog, it would take a human expert an enormous amount of time to manually evaluate and prioritize the most relevant attributes for each accessory pairing. We solved this by using LLMs to automatically analyze the product data, identify the most important attributes, and assign them importance weights for various pairs of core (or seed) and accessory item types. (Figure 1) For instance, when recommending pillowcases as accessories for sheet sets (see Figure 1), color and material are treated as the most significant factors. In contrast, when suggesting an appropriate book to accompany a kids' craft activity kit, the intended audience attribute (infant, kids, adults, etc.) becomes the most important consideration. The model formulates scoring rules using LLMs and uses them to compute scores for all accessory items. When a core item’s attribute value matches an accessory item’s attribute value, the attribute weight is added to the accessory item relevance score. Ultimately, the accessory items with the highest scores are selected as final recommendations (sales rank serves as a tie-breaking mechanism in cases where scores are equal). 2. Capturing Aesthetic Matches: The second challenge involves situations where the matching requires an aesthetic sense. For these pairings, it is insufficient to recommend items whose attributes match—we must also consider how they coordinate together as part of a complete set. We serendipitously discovered that the LLM was quite good at using concepts like color harmony and stylistic coherence. (Figure 2) (Figure 3) For instance, in Figures 2 and 3, the LLM uses attributes such as color, material, and style to create harmonious sets of attribute values that enable more diverse and creative recommendations. This holistic approach significantly enhances our accessory suggestions, resulting in visually appealing and cohesive arrangements. 3. Scaling Across Large Catalogs: With hundreds of thousands of items in the Home category, it was crucial that our algorithm scale effectively. To do so, we constrained the algorithm to only consider attributes for pairs of core and accessory item types , rather than pairs of the items themselves. This vastly reduced time and cost complexity. Also, once scoring rules were established for each pair of core and accessory item types, the model needed only to score and sort all pairs of items in those types (an operation we also parallelized). The resulting algorithm is scalable enough that we foresee it will be easy to adapt it to categories beyond Home. Integration with Human Insight Although the model was effective as described, we made sure to include human-in-the-loop (HITL) processes to solidify the recommendations. Specifically, we collaborated with site merchants to create a list of the most commonly co-purchased accessory items, enabling support for cross-category recommendations. As can be seen in Figures 4-6, the mode without HITL frequently suggests similar items, whereas employing HITL led to accessory recommendations from a far more diverse set of items. This is quite useful, because the model without HITL can be used effectively by guests who are still in the exploration stage (comparing similar accessories), while the model with HITL ends up facilitating basket expansion by exposing guests to a far wider array of accessory types based on what is already in their carts. (Figure 4) (Figure 5) (Figure 6) Results from A/B Testing In February 2025, we conducted an A/B test where we added the Home Accessory model to the add-to-cart flyout. This resulted in the following boost to our business metrics: Around an 11% increase in interaction rate indicating heightened engagement A roughly 12% increase in display-to-conversion rates reflecting stronger content relevance and downstream impact More than 9% growth in attributable demand In summary, by combining both LLMs and human insights into a single capability, we have transformed the way accessories can be recommended at Target across diverse categories. This comprehensive system not only enhances user engagement but also facilitates seamless shopping experiences. We are excited to announce that this model was fully rolled out to production in April 2025, marking a significant milestone in our commitment to delivering exceptional value and convenience for our customers.
